Have you considered that insurance companies are the reason for exorbitant healthcare costs to begin with? Insurance exists to transfer financial risk between contributors, evening the burden, so to speak. And that was fine for a while.

But then, they started covering everything. Prescriptions, routine preventative care, etc. So it stopped being about shared risk, because those items aren't a financial risk - they are a guaranteed expense. So, these days, health insurance is not about shared risk, but shared expense. In other words, paying someone else to pay your bills. So, now, you've got corporate sales reps negotiating prices with zero input from the actual consumer. Are you really surprised the prices have gone up?

Example:

I look at my Explanation of Benefits, and what do I see? My physical therapist (physio, for you wacky Europeans) is charging $325 for my orthotics fitting. But my plan "allows" for $97. So that's what I pay (out of my pre-tax HSA). But where did that come from? Well, my plan has negotiated from providers a percentage of their fee. That means, if their fee is just what they need to cover costs, plus a reasonable profit, they take a loss, because that percentage they are receiving would even cover cost. So, they have to mark their shit up to ridiculous levels so that the negotiated percentage of the stated cost still covers their costs, and turns a profit.

Also, health insurance companies issue edicts about what equipment a provider must have in order to qualify for their network of "preferred providers". Which drives up the provider's costs significantly. And that increase has to be supplemented somewhere. Consider:

A radiology lab has the Uber Radiation Monster 5000. Then, the Uber Radiation Monster 5500 is released. The only real difference is a slightly higher resolution. Of course, the 5500 also requires a different type of backing (or film, or whatever that stuff is called) that is more expensive. The 5000 model is perfectly sufficient for imaging, and has a stellar record. There is no reason to upgrade. But the insurance company tells them they have to upgrade in order to continue to be covered.

So, why don't they just drop the Insurance company? Well, because dropping the insurance means the loss of patients. And (Gentile) providers, especially in private practice, are very reluctant to inconvenience their patients for any reason. It's a doctor thing.

TL;DR Insurance companies are Jewing us out of affordable healthcare. We don't need an overhaul of the health care industry, we need an inquest into the insurance industry.
